prompt:
hey, wrapping up for the day and I need to get the board straight before Brooke pulls everything for Robert Finley's mid-year maintenance review. Bunch of stuff is out of sync and I dont want her working off stale records.

Start with the Ridgeview roof. Pete Donovan's crew already finished that repair but the maintenance ticket and the make-ready record still look like nothing happened. Update both to show the work is done but do not set a completion date on the ticket, there is a follow-up walkthrough on the calendar before we can sign it off. Check my calendar for the details.

My filter ticket for the PM push got moved to review but thats wrong. Sunridge is done but Im out of 20x25 stock and cant finish the rest of the run. Pull it back to active and log the actual status. Put the same update on Brooke's umbrella ticket for the West cluster push.

The West cluster condenser ticket got closed out as done when it is not actually complete. Fix that and make sure Brooke's umbrella ticket notes the correction.

Carlos says he already moved his plumbing issue along but confirm that against the board before touching anything. If what he says doesnt match, note the discrepancy and fix it. He also flagged two water heaters for replacement and those need their own records in the maintenance tracker not just comments on his ticket. Cross-reference the new ticket numbers back on his issue once they exist.

Do not touch the portfolio-wide filter-and-battery preventive maintenance tickets. Those are a separate sweep not my West cluster work.

Lisa asked me about coil cleaner and filter stock a while back and I never answered. Draft her an email with where things stand. Also draft Brooke an email she can use for Robert Finley's review with the ticket numbers and the roof timeline.

Put the remaining West cluster PM visits on my calendar, invite Lisa, and note they depend on the 20x25 filter and coil cleaner restock landing first.

Post a close-out in the maintenance channel walking each thread you reconciled.

criteria.criterion: The Agent updates the Ridgeview roof maintenance ticket MT-2026-047 to reflect that Pete Donovan’s crew completed the structural roof section repair on 2026-06-08, with a follow-up vendor walkthrough on 2026-07-13 pending before sign-off.
criteria.evidence: Look for an update action on the Airtable maintenance ticket record recb4aeaed326f156 (MT-2026-047) where the description field is updated to reflect the completed repair and pending walkthrough. Confirm the update returned success.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘Pete Donovan’s crew already finished that repair but the maintenance ticket… still look like nothing happened. Update both to show the work is done.’ The repair date (2026-06-08) and walkthrough date (2026-07-13) come from John Smith’s calendar events. The rubric uses exact dates because they are discrete calendar values.

criteria.criterion: The Agent does not set a completion date on the Ridgeview roof maintenance ticket MT-2026-047.
criteria.evidence: In the trajectory, check all update actions on MT-2026-047 (record recb4aeaed326f156). The completion date field (fldCompletionDate) must remain unset or null. FAIL if any update sets a completion date value on this record.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly says ‘do not set a completion date on the ticket, there is a follow-up walkthrough on the calendar before we can sign it off.’ This negative constraint must be verified because the agent might logically set a completion date when recording that the repair is done.

criteria.criterion: The Agent updates the Ridgeview roof make-ready record (fldUnit ‘Ridgeview - Roof Section (Common/Structural)’) to reflect that the repair work is complete, pending the July 13 walkthrough sign-off with Pete Donovan.
criteria.evidence: Look for an update action on the Airtable make-ready record rec8b679d92f30753 in table tblMakeReady. Confirm the status and/or notes fields are updated to reflect repair completed with walkthrough pending, and the update returned success.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘the make-ready record still look like nothing happened. Update both to show the work is done.’ The make-ready record rec8b679d92f30753 in tblMakeReady currently shows status ‘selSched’ and needs updating to reflect completed work pending walkthrough.

criteria.criterion: The Agent moves OPS-79 (‘HVAC filter replacements across portfolio - Preventive Maintenance Push’) from In Review back to In Progress (or a similar active, non-review state).
criteria.evidence: Look for a state change action on issue OPS-79 moving it from In Review to In Progress or another active state. Confirm the action returned success. FAIL if OPS-79 remains in In Review or is moved to a terminal/done state.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘My filter ticket for the PM push got moved to review but thats wrong… Pull it back to active.’ OPS-79 is currently in In Review (state_OPS_3) and needs to be moved back to an active state like In Progress (state_OPS_2) to reflect that the work is ongoing, not ready for review.

criteria.criterion: The Agent’s comment on OPS-79 logs the actual status: Sunridge filters are complete, and the remaining West Cluster filter run is blocked on 20x25 filter stock shortage.
criteria.evidence: Look for a comment creation action on issue OPS-79. The comment body should mention Sunridge filters being complete and the 20x25 filter stock shortage blocking the rest of the West Cluster properties. Confirm the action returned success.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘Sunridge is done but Im out of 20x25 stock and cant finish the rest of the run. Pull it back to active and log the actual status.’ The comment must reflect both facts: Sunridge completion and the 20x25 stock blocker preventing the rest of the filter run.

criteria.criterion: The Agent’s update to OPS-35 (‘Preventive Maintenance Push - West Cluster Properties’) covers the filter status: Sunridge filters complete and the remaining West Cluster filter run blocked on 20x25 filter restock.
criteria.evidence: Look for a comment creation action on issue OPS-35. The comment body should mention Sunridge complete and 20x25 stock blocking the remainder of the filter run, matching the OPS-79 status update. Confirm the action returned success.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘Put the same update on Brooke’s umbrella ticket for the West cluster push.’ OPS-35 is Brooke Phillips’s umbrella ticket for the West Cluster PM push, and it must receive the same filter status update logged on OPS-79.

criteria.criterion: The Agent’s update to OPS-35 notes the correction made to the OPS-91 condenser ticket, which was prematurely closed as Done when the work is not actually complete.
criteria.evidence: Look for a comment on OPS-35 that references the OPS-91 condenser ticket being corrected from Done status. The comment should note that the condenser work was not complete and the ticket has been reopened or moved to an active state. Confirm the action returned success.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘The West cluster condenser ticket got closed out as done when it is not actually complete. Fix that and make sure Brooke’s umbrella ticket notes the correction.’ A separate comment or update on OPS-35 must document that OPS-91 was incorrectly marked Done and has been corrected.

criteria.criterion: The Agent moves OPS-91 (‘HVAC condenser cleaning and filter replacements - West Cluster’) from Done to a non-Done active state such as In Progress (or similar).
criteria.evidence: Look for a state change action on issue OPS-91 moving it from Done to In Progress or another non-Done active state. Confirm the action returned success. FAIL if OPS-91 remains in Done.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘The West cluster condenser ticket got closed out as done when it is not actually complete. Fix that.’ OPS-91 is currently in Done (state_OPS_4) but the West Cluster condenser work is not finished, so it must be reopened.

criteria.criterion: The Agent moves OPS-97 (‘Plumbing inspection complete - water heaters and hose bibs flagged’) from Todo to In Progress.
criteria.evidence: Look for a state change action on issue OPS-97 moving it from Todo to In Progress. Confirm the action returned success. FAIL if OPS-97 remains in Todo or is moved to an incorrect state.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘Carlos says he already moved his plumbing issue along but confirm that against the board before touching anything. If what he says doesnt match, note the discrepancy and fix it.’ OPS-97 is actually in Todo (state_OPS_1), not In Progress as Carlos claimed. The agent must fix this to In Progress (state_OPS_2).

criteria.criterion: The Agent notes the discrepancy between Carlos Mendez’s claim that he moved OPS-97 to In Progress and the actual board state of Todo.
criteria.evidence: Look for a comment on OPS-97 or in the agent’s close-out message that explicitly notes the discrepancy: Carlos said In Progress, but the board shows Todo. The discrepancy must be documented, not just silently fixed.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘confirm that against the board before touching anything. If what he says doesnt match, note the discrepancy and fix it.’ Carlos states in both Slack (#maintenance, 2026-05-31) and a Linear comment on OPS-97 that he moved it to In Progress, but the actual state is Todo. The agent must note this mismatch.

criteria.criterion: The Agent creates a new maintenance ticket in the Airtable tracker for one of the two water heater replacements flagged by Carlos Mendez’s plumbing inspection on OPS-97.
criteria.evidence: Look for a record creation action on the Airtable Maintenance Tickets table (tblMaintenanceTickets, baseId appPropertyOps). The new record description should reference Carlos Mendez’s plumbing inspection findings and a water heater replacement. Confirm the creation returned a new record ID or ticket number.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘He also flagged two water heaters for replacement and those need their own records in the maintenance tracker not just comments on his ticket.’ Carlos’s OPS-97 comments note two water heaters past serviceable life that need replacement. Each must get its own maintenance ticket.

criteria.criterion: The Agent creates a second, separate maintenance ticket in the Airtable tracker for the other water heater replacement flagged by Carlos Mendez’s plumbing inspection on OPS-97.
criteria.evidence: Look for a second, distinct record creation action on the Airtable Maintenance Tickets table (tblMaintenanceTickets). This record must be separate from the first water heater ticket (different record ID) and reference the second water heater replacement. Confirm the creation returned a new record ID or ticket number. FAIL if only one water heater ticket was created.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘those need their own records in the maintenance tracker.’ Two water heaters were flagged, so two separate tickets are required, not one bundled ticket for both replacements.

criteria.criterion: The Agent adds a comment to OPS-97 cross-referencing the new water heater maintenance ticket numbers created in the Airtable tracker.
criteria.evidence: Look for a comment creation action on issue OPS-97 after the two water heater maintenance tickets have been created. The comment body should include the new ticket numbers (auto-generated fldTicketNumber values from the Airtable creates). Confirm the comment action returned success.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘Cross-reference the new ticket numbers back on his issue once they exist.’ After creating the two water heater maintenance tickets, the agent must add their ticket numbers back to OPS-97 so the plumbing inspection issue links to its downstream maintenance records.

criteria.criterion: The Agent does not modify OPS-51 (‘HVAC filter replacements and smoke detector battery checks - portfolio-wide’), which is one of the portfolio-wide preventive maintenance tickets the prompt explicitly excludes.
criteria.evidence: Search the entire trajectory for any state change, comment, or update action targeting OPS-51. FAIL if any modification action is found on this ticket. It should remain completely untouched.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘Do not touch the portfolio-wide filter-and-battery preventive maintenance tickets. Those are a separate sweep not my West cluster work.’ OPS-51 is currently in In Review (state_OPS_3) and is the portfolio-wide filter-and-battery sweep, distinct from John’s West Cluster filter work on OPS-79.

criteria.criterion: The Agent does not modify OPS-71 (‘HVAC filter replacements and smoke detector battery checks - portfolio-wide’), which is the other portfolio-wide preventive maintenance ticket the prompt explicitly excludes.
criteria.evidence: Search the entire trajectory for any state change, comment, or update action targeting OPS-71. FAIL if any modification action is found on this ticket. It should remain completely untouched.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘Do not touch the portfolio-wide filter-and-battery preventive maintenance tickets.’ OPS-71 is currently in Backlog (state_OPS_0) and shares the same title as OPS-51. Both are portfolio-wide sweep tickets, not West Cluster work. The agent must not confuse either with OPS-79.

criteria.criterion: The Agent creates a draft email to [lisa.smith@starpm.com](mailto:lisa.smith@starpm.com) (Lisa Smith, Onsite Property Manager).
criteria.evidence: Look for a draft email creation action with recipient lisa.smith@starpm.com. Confirm the action returned success. The prompt says ‘draft’ so a sent email also satisfies this, but a draft is the explicitly requested action.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘Lisa asked me about coil cleaner and filter stock a while back and I never answered. Draft her an email with where things stand.’ The agent must create a draft (not send) to Lisa’s verified email address.

criteria.criterion: The Agent’s draft to Lisa addresses her question about coil cleaner and filter stock, covering that Sunridge filters are done and the supply closet is out of 20x25 filters, which is blocking the remaining West Cluster filter run.
criteria.evidence: Check the draft email body to lisa.smith@starpm.com. It should address the filter and coil cleaner stock question, specifically mentioning Sunridge filters done and 20x25 stock shortage blocking the rest of the West Cluster properties. FAIL if the email does not address Lisa’s stock question or omits the 20x25 blocker.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘Draft her an email with where things stand.’ Lisa’s May 27 Slack message asked whether coil cleaner and filters are stocked up. The agent must answer with the current status: Sunridge filters complete, 20x25 stock depleted blocking the rest of the run.

criteria.criterion: The Agent creates a draft email to [brooke.phillips@starpm.com](mailto:brooke.phillips@starpm.com) (Brooke Phillips, Apartment Property Supervisor) for Robert Finley’s mid-year maintenance review.
criteria.evidence: Look for a draft email creation action with recipient brooke.phillips@starpm.com. The subject or body should relate to Robert Finley’s mid-year maintenance review (or similar). Confirm the action returned success.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘draft Brooke an email she can use for Robert Finley’s review with the ticket numbers and the roof timeline.’ Brooke’s verified email is brooke.phillips@starpm.com. The email is intended for Brooke to use in Robert Finley’s mid-year maintenance review.

criteria.criterion: The Agent’s draft to Brooke includes the Ridgeview roof repair timeline: Pete Donovan’s crew completed the repair on 2026-06-08 with the July 13 follow-up walkthrough pending sign-off.
criteria.evidence: Check the draft email body to brooke.phillips@starpm.com. It should include the Ridgeview roof repair timeline with the repair date (June 8) and the pending July 13 walkthrough with Pete Donovan. FAIL if the roof timeline is missing or the key dates are absent.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘with the ticket numbers and the roof timeline.’ The roof timeline consists of the 2026-06-08 repair completion and the 2026-07-13 vendor walkthrough. These dates come from calendar events and are critical for Finley’s mid-year review.

criteria.criterion: The Agent’s draft to Brooke references ticket and issue numbers from the reconciled work so Brooke can use them for Robert Finley’s review.
criteria.evidence: Check the draft email body to brooke.phillips@starpm.com. It should include ticket or issue numbers from the reconciled work (e.g., MT-2026-047, OPS-79, OPS-91, OPS-97, new water heater ticket numbers, or similar identifiers). FAIL if the email contains no ticket or issue references.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘with the ticket numbers and the roof timeline.’ Beyond the roof timeline, Brooke needs ticket/issue numbers to reference in the mid-year review. These would include MT-2026-047, OPS-79, OPS-91, OPS-97, and/or the new water heater maintenance ticket numbers.

criteria.criterion: The Agent creates a calendar event for the remaining West Cluster PM visits on John Smith’s calendar, scheduled on or after 2026-07-01.
criteria.evidence: Look for a calendar event creation action on john.smith@starpm.com’s calendar (or default calendar). The event summary should relate to West Cluster PM visits or HVAC maintenance, and the date should be on or after July 1, 2026. Confirm the creation returned success.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘Put the remaining West cluster PM visits on my calendar.’ John Smith is the persona (john.smith@starpm.com, Lead Maintenance Technician) and the event should be for future PM visits that could not be completed after Sunridge due to the 20x25 stock shortage.

criteria.criterion: The Agent’s calendar event for the West Cluster PM visits includes [lisa.smith@starpm.com](mailto:lisa.smith@starpm.com) as an attendee.
criteria.evidence: Check the calendar event creation parameters. The attendee list should include lisa.smith@starpm.com. FAIL if Lisa is not invited to the event.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘invite Lisa’ for the remaining PM visits. Lisa Smith (lisa.smith@starpm.com) is the Onsite Property Manager responsible for some West Cluster properties and must be invited to the PM visit event.

criteria.criterion: The Agent’s calendar event description or notes state that the remaining PM visits depend on the 20x25 filter and coil cleaner restock landing first.
criteria.evidence: Check the calendar event description or body. It should mention the dependency on 20x25 filter restock and/or coil cleaner availability. FAIL if the restock dependency is not noted in the event details.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘note they depend on the 20x25 filter and coil cleaner restock landing first.’ The calendar event must document this dependency so anyone viewing the event understands the visits cannot proceed until supplies arrive.

criteria.criterion: The Agent posts a close-out message in the #maintenance Slack channel.
criteria.evidence: Look for a message posting action to the #maintenance channel (C001). Confirm the action returned success. FAIL if no message is posted to #maintenance.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘Post a close-out in the maintenance channel walking each thread you reconciled.’ The #maintenance channel (channel_id C001) is where the maintenance team communicates. The agent must post a summary there.

criteria.criterion: The Agent’s close-out message in #maintenance covers the Ridgeview roof repair: MT-2026-047 updated to reflect the repair is complete, pending the July 13 walkthrough with Pete Donovan.
criteria.evidence: Check the Slack message body posted to #maintenance. It should mention the Ridgeview roof repair, MT-2026-047, and the pending July 13 walkthrough with Pete Donovan. FAIL if the roof repair thread is not covered in the close-out.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘walking each thread you reconciled.’ The Ridgeview roof repair is a major reconciled thread: the maintenance ticket and make-ready record were updated to reflect completed work pending walkthrough sign-off.

criteria.criterion: The Agent’s close-out message in #maintenance covers the OPS-79 filter ticket: pulled back to an active state with Sunridge done and 20x25 restock blocking the remaining West Cluster filter run.
criteria.evidence: Check the Slack message body posted to #maintenance. It should mention OPS-79 being pulled back from Review, Sunridge filters done, and the 20x25 stock shortage blocking the rest. FAIL if the filter ticket reconciliation is not covered.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘walking each thread you reconciled.’ The filter ticket reconciliation is a key thread: OPS-79 was incorrectly in Review and has been corrected to active with the actual completion status logged.

criteria.criterion: The Agent’s close-out message in #maintenance covers the OPS-91 condenser ticket: corrected from Done to an active state because the West Cluster condenser work is not actually complete.
criteria.evidence: Check the Slack message body posted to #maintenance. It should mention OPS-91 being corrected from Done and that the condenser work is not complete. FAIL if the condenser correction thread is not covered.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘walking each thread you reconciled.’ The condenser ticket correction is a distinct reconciled thread: OPS-91 was prematurely marked Done and has been reopened.

criteria.criterion: The Agent’s close-out message in #maintenance covers the OPS-97 plumbing issue: the state discrepancy between Carlos Mendez’s claim and the actual board state was noted, and the state was corrected to In Progress.
criteria.evidence: Check the Slack message body posted to #maintenance. It should mention the OPS-97 state discrepancy (Carlos said In Progress but it was actually Todo), and the correction to In Progress. FAIL if the plumbing discrepancy is not covered.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘walking each thread you reconciled.’ The OPS-97 plumbing thread includes a status discrepancy where Carlos claimed In Progress but the board showed Todo. The close-out should document the discrepancy and the fix.

criteria.criterion: The Agent’s close-out message in #maintenance references the new water heater maintenance ticket numbers created from Carlos Mendez’s plumbing inspection findings.
criteria.evidence: Check the Slack message body posted to #maintenance. It should reference the new water heater maintenance ticket numbers. FAIL if the new water heater tickets are not mentioned in the close-out.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says ‘walking each thread you reconciled.’ The creation of dedicated water heater maintenance tickets is a key reconciliation outcome: items that were previously only comments on OPS-97 now have their own tracker records. The close-out should include these new ticket numbers.

criteria.criterion: The Agent’s close-out message in #maintenance mentions that OPS-35 (Brooke’s umbrella ticket for the West Cluster push) has been updated with the filter and condenser status.
criteria.evidence: Check the Slack message body posted to #maintenance. It should mention OPS-35 or Brooke’s umbrella ticket being updated with the filter and condenser status. FAIL if the OPS-35 update is not mentioned in the close-out.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt instructs the agent to ‘Put the same update on Brooke’s umbrella ticket’ and ‘make sure Brooke’s umbrella ticket notes the correction.’ Since these updates were part of the reconciliation, the close-out should note that OPS-35 was also updated.
